title: Shobna Gulati & Christina Bianco in The Rise and Fall of Little Voice - review
transcript: the touring production of the rise and fall of little voice starring christina bianco shobna gulati and ian kelsey which i saw at the mast in southampton touring productions are the cinderella of british theater given the choice actors will often prefer to work in one place preferably london and so when i saw that two former soap actors and a youtube sensation were heading the cast of the new touring production of the rise and fall of little voice i feared the worst how wrong i was jim cartwright's play about an introverted young woman mourning her father and badly treated by her mother who finds escape in the music of classic female singers has been revived many times and was made into a memorable film so in some ways the challenge is not to mess it up but shobna gelati is the horrendous mother mary is hilarious ian kelsey is the smooth talking showbiz manager gives us just the right mix of sleaziness and desperation and as for christina bianco as the taciturn daughter with the voice of an angel well i have a lot to say about her but that's the one minute up so keep watching for much more about this excellent production of the rise and fall of little voice let's start with christina bianco i've never heard of her till now which is clearly my bad since she has 123 000 followers on youtube and her impressions of singers have been viewed over 25 million times now the problem for all the actors in this show is that there has been a definitive film version that is imprinted on most of us brenda blethin as mary the mother michael kane as ray the small-time talent agent and of course jane horrocks as lv or little voice so they all have to work very hard to make you forget those definitive performances not more so than the person playing lv and the first question is how well can she sing we get glimpses as the first act progresses and then there are two nightclub performances which lv has pushed into making does christina bianca carry it off she most certainly does not only does she sing beautifully but her impressions of judy garland marilyn monroe shirley bassey and many more are spot on i mean after all these years very few in the audience will be surprised when after all the silence and whispers lv reveals her diva singing voice but the tingle down the back of the neck that miss bianco creates is still powerful enough to merit a round of appreciative applause if you want a taste of how good christina bianco is at impressions of singers watch her on youtube singing let it go there's a choice but i'd recommend the video from about a year ago as for her lancashire accent well okay she's an impressionist but it's just right you'd never know she's from new york she's uncannily like jane horrocks but i think it would be unfair to dismiss her performance as simply an impression since jim cartwright wrote the part of lv for jane horrocks and she played it both in its national theater premiere and on film it's arguable there's little leeway for playing it differently in other words that's how the part is meant to be played the important thing is christina bianco is entirely convincing that someone traumatized by grief and parental abuse who continues to be bullied until she finds her own voice then there's the rest of the cast with the part of maori jim cartwright created one of theater's great monsters a selfish woman with no redeeming features whose only concern is her own love life and who abuses not only her daughter but the english language shodner galati grabs the part with both hands and extracts every ounce of comedy out of it she relishes the outrageous puns i did it my way and and dishes out her malapropisms such as she can't even be swivel or at my time of strife with a perfect deadpan delivery visually her tasteless outfits and makeup are so over the top that many drag acts would find it hard to compete and her physical comedy is a joy especially when she's playing being drunk i loved the moment when she pulled ian kelsey onto the sofa her legs flailing in the air she does literally throw herself into the role and gives it as her character would say one hundred percenters andy and kelsey is a revelation i last saw him 30 years ago as danny zuko in greece he's still offering roguish allure but here as he attempts to exploit lv he adds an underlying nastiness mr kelsey conveys well the ageing charm and sense of failure that make his character so comically pathetic fiona mulvaney is excellent as mary's friend sadie although i can't help feeling the part of a stooge who says very little other than okay is uh reminiscent of the kind of one-dimensional character you'd find in an old-fashioned sitcom and that's just one of the ways this play is now showing its age uh also this mainly pacey play seemed to be to be drawn out at the end the set designed by sarah perks takes the form of a two-up two-down house with the front and part of the roof torn off as if giving us an unauthorized glimpse into what would normally go on behind closed doors it's crowded with furniture and other cheap objects adding to a strong sense of marie's tawdryness and the claustrophobia of working class life broner largan is the director responsible for a production that gives laughter pathos and joy in equal measures i give her touring production of the rise and fall of little voice four stars i hope you found this review interesting if you did and you want to be the first to know about my future reviews please subscribe costs nothing and if reading reviews is more your thing please visit one minute theater reviews dot co dot uk thank you for watching
